summary: Siuslaw NF peak east of Florence, OR: 1934 tower, 41-ft L-4 tower from 1954, used for emergencies in the 1970s, now gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Used for emergency in the 1970s, now gone per the register and firelookout.com; no source describes remains

staffing.status: Forest Service crew maintained the lookout in 1941; Aircraft Warning Service station activated 1942

events.note: Register: 30-foot L-4 tower built; Rex's: 50-foot round timber tower with 14x14 L-4 cab. A June 8, 1934 Siuslaw Oar item says the tower would be built once a road extended by a Sweets Creek CCC side camp was far enough along to bring in supplies
Five-person Forest Service crew did general maintenance, including lightning protection
Aircraft Warning Service station activated August 12, 1942 (Eugene Filter Center)
firelookout.com lists a 30-foot L-4 tower under 1942 (the register and Rex's give 1934 for the first tower)
41-foot treated timber L-4 tower replaces the first tower (treated timber per register and firelookout.com; Rex's says timber)
Used for emergencies in the 1970s (decade only)
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on December 18, 2010

corrections.why: 15.2 m is 50 feet, which matches only the 1934 tower on Rex's page. The register and firelookout.com give 41 feet for the 1954 tower, the last one built, which is about 12.5 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives a 30-foot L-4 tower for 1934. firelookout.com lists a 30-foot L-4 tower too, but dates it to 1942, not 1934. Rex's page gives a 50-foot round timber structure with a 14x14 L-4 cab for 1934. All three agree that the 1954 tower was 41 feet.

notes_for_editor: No source gives an access level or describes the site today, so facts.access is omitted. The brief's height_m of 15.2 m (50 ft) is proposed for correction to 12.5 m (41 ft, the 1954 tower). A peakery.com search snippet gave 1,621 ft for the summit; it is not used because it conflicts with the register's 1,826 ft and is not a lookout source.
